Scope note: assessment is limited strictly to facts supplied. Nothing is assumed beyond them.

BUT the FNOL date to the carrier is NOT supplied - cannot assume the carrier was unaware. Only DOL-to-intake is known.                Actual FNOL date and method (EV-05); any earlier correspondence (EV-08)
                                         Loss close to policy expiration                    PARTIAL - SOFT                           Loss fell 46 days before expiry (2024-12-31). --- B. DAMAGE SIGNAL CONSISTENCY CHECK ---
                     Reported damage element               Consistent with stated cause?                                                                                                                                                                   Basis                                                                         Corroboration required                                                                                             Review note
         Flooring - water damage to flooring                       Consistent with cause                                                                                         Escape of water onto a floor is a direct, expected consequence of a burst pipe. Moisture map + flooring material (EV-15/18) to confirm extent vs. replacement of entire floor.                       Scope may include undamaged areas if entire floor replaced - allocation question.
           Drywall - water damage to drywall                       Consistent with cause                                                                                                  Water migration into wall cavities and wicking up drywall is expected.                                  Photo evidence + moisture readings at wall height (EV-14/15).                     Wicking height should correlate with volume and duration; check 'flood cut' height.
           Inventory - water damage to stock Consistent only if geographically plausible                                                                                  Inventory is only directly damaged if stored in or adjacent to the affected back room.                         Inventory list with storage location + aisle/rack (EV-19); floor plan. If stock is stored elsewhere (front of store), direct water damage is questionable - needs explanation.
Multiple building systems / widespread scope                                  Watch item Three separate property classes (floor, wall, contents) can all be expected from one event, but the combined scope should be proportionate to a single-room pipe burst.                                                         Itemized scope + photos (EV-17/18/14).                             Oversized scope relative to a 'back room' origin would be a review trigger.
       Reported speed / duration of exposure                          Unknown - critical               The description says 'burst' (sudden). The 23-month reporting gap raises the question of whether water actually flowed undetected for an extended period.                              Mitigation date stamp; drying logs; cause & origin (EV-23/24/09).  Sudden burst vs. prolonged escape changes which exclusion applies - this is the pivotal damage signal.
                          Causation timeline                                     Unknown                                                                           No date-stamped evidence ties the damage to 2024-11-15 rather than a later or earlier period.                                Date-stamped photos, plumber report, POS records (EV-14/09/32).                              Damage dating must be corroborated independently of the insured's account.
                 Repair vs. replace approach                                     Unknown                                                                                        Whether damaged items are being repaired or replaced drives RCV/ACV and salvage.                                             Contractor estimates + valuation basis (EV-17/20).                                             Consider salvage/subrogation offsets on replaced inventory.

--- C. SUBROGATION OPPORTUNITY MATRIX ---
                                            Subrogation theory                                            Legal basis                                                                       Target party                                                                              Evidence required                                                      Current viability                                                                                        Blocker / caveat
                       Defective plumbing repair / workmanship            Negligence / breach of contract or warranty Third-party contractor or plumber whose work caused or contributed to the rupture. Work order, invoice, contract, cause & origin attribution to the repair (EV-29, EV-40, EV-09).  CONDITIONAL - no repair is known to have occurred; cannot assume one.                     No third party identified yet; 22-month delay may have replaced the failed section.
                                     Landlord / premises owner Landlord's contractual duty to maintain, or negligence            If the claimant is a tenant and the failed pipe is landlord-maintained.                             Lease agreement allocating maintenance; ownership records (EV-37).  UNKNOWN - ownership vs. leasehold not supplied; cannot assume either.                                                 Only arises if claimant is not the sole owner-occupant.
                Manufacturer / supplier of the pipe or fitting Product liability (WA Product Liability Act, RCW 7.72)                           Defect in manufacture or design of the failed component. Artifact almost certainly lost after 22 months; statute of repose and spoliation both cut against this.
                       Adjoining tenant or third-party utility                                             Negligence               Third party caused the pipe to fail or water from elsewhere entered.                         Evidence of third-party activity; camera/borescope inspection (EV-11).                SPECULATIVE - no fact supplied points to a third party.                                                                         Do not pursue without evidence.

N/A.                                                                    N/A If freeze is established, it removes subrogation but also raises the freeze exclusion against coverage.

N/A                                                               This is a coverage issue, not a recovery.
